Never wake up empty-handed.

gnhf is a [ralph](https://ghuntley.com/ralph/), [autoresearch](https://github.com/karpathy/autoresearch)-style orchestrator that keeps your agents running while you sleep — each iteration makes one small, committed, documented change towards an objective.
You wake up to a branch full of clean work and a log of everything that happened.

- **Dead simple** — one command starts an autonomous loop that runs until you request stop or a configured runtime cap is reached
- **Long running** — each iteration is committed on success, rolled back on failure except commit failures preserved for repair, with sensible retries; retryable hard agent errors back off exponentially while agent-reported failures continue immediately
- **Live terminal title** — interactive runs keep your terminal title updated with live status, token totals, and commit count, then clear or restore it on exit depending on terminal support; token totals prefixed with `~` are estimates
- **Exit summary**: every run ends with a permanent summary covering elapsed time, branch, iterations, tokens, branch diff stats, local notes/log paths, and review commands
- **Agent-agnostic**: works with Claude Code, Codex, Rovo Dev, OpenCode, GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi, or ACP targets out of the box

## Quick Start

```sh
$ gnhf "reduce complexity of the codebase without changing functionality"
# have a good sleep
```

```sh
$ gnhf "reduce complexity of the codebase without changing functionality" \
    --max-iterations 10 \
    --max-tokens 5000000
# have a good nap
```

```sh
# Run multiple agents on the same repo simultaneously using worktrees
$ gnhf --worktree "implement feature X" &
$ gnhf --worktree "add tests for module Y" &
$ gnhf --worktree "refactor the API layer" &
```

```sh
# Commit directly on the current branch and push after each successful iteration
$ gnhf --current-branch --push "keep improving this app"
```

Run `gnhf` from inside a Git repository with a clean working tree. If you are starting from a plain directory, run `git init` first.
`gnhf` supports macOS, Linux, and Windows.

## Install

**npm**

```sh
npm install -g gnhf
```

**From source**

```sh
git clone https://github.com/kunchenguid/gnhf.git
cd gnhf
npm install
npm run build
npm link
```

# deadreckon

**The control plane for unattended agentic coding CLIs.**

deadreckon runs long coding tasks the way you wish agentic CLIs already did: in an isolated workspace, with durable state, live attach, spend and wall-clock caps, per-turn undo, provenance, traces, self-documenting run artifacts, and a signed acceptance gate before anything is promoted.

It is not trying to out-code Amp, Rovo Dev, Cursor CLI, Codex, Claude Code, Aider, deepseek-tui, GitHub Copilot CLI, or the next terminal agent. Use the agentic CLI you already trust. deadreckon wraps it in the missing operational harness.

```bash
deadreckon run "replace the legacy billing flow with Stripe Checkout"
deadreckon attach latest
deadreckon status
deadreckon doc latest
deadreckon apply latest --autostash --cleanup
```

## Why "deadreckon"?

Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: start from a known
position, keep a continuous record of movement, and use that record to know
where you are now.

That is the problem with unattended coding agents. The model is probabilistic,
the task can run for a long time, context is partial, and the terminal may be
gone by the time you inspect the result. deadreckon keeps the course anyway:
every turn writes state, spend, traces, provenance, snapshots, docs, and
acceptance evidence.

The name is the contract: do not trust a final answer alone. Navigate agent work
by evidence.

## Why This Exists

Agentic coding CLIs are good at the inner loop: talk to a model, inspect files, run commands, edit code, and produce a patch. Amp, Rovo Dev, Cursor CLI, Codex, Claude Code, Aider, deepseek-tui, GitHub Copilot CLI, and similar tools are racing on model UX, tool UX, context handling, and terminal/editor ergonomics.

deadreckon focuses on the layer around that CLI: the unattended run lifecycle.

The painful part of unattended coding is different:

- Where exactly did the agent run?
- What did it spend?
- Which files did each turn touch?
- Can I attach after closing my laptop?
- Can I kill it without leaving orphaned processes?
- Can I resume after a crash?
- Can I undo turn 7 without rolling back the whole project?
- Can I prove the agent did not mark its own work as accepted?
- Can I apply the result only after I inspect it?

deadreckon is built around those questions. It treats an agentic CLI as the worker, then adds the control plane that makes unattended work reviewable, recoverable, auditable, and safe to apply.

## The Printing Press Contract

deadreckon borrows a simple idea from the CLI Printing Press pattern: split
judgment from enforcement.

The agentic CLI and Markdown skills own the judgment layer: what to inspect,
what to try, what to edit, and when to say the work is done. The Rust binary owns
the enforcement layer: state, locks, sandboxes, provider routing, cancellation,
snapshots, provenance, spend, traces, gates, promotion, and recovery.

That split matters. The agent can write code, but it cannot forge completion,
skip the audit trail, bypass run state, or silently publish its own work.

## The Unique Feature Set

### Isolated Worktrees By Default

In a git repo, `deadreckon run` creates a separate `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch under `~/.deadreckon/worktrees/`. Your checkout is left untouched until you explicitly run:

```bash
deadreckon apply <run-id>
```

Run ids accept unique prefixes, and most commands also accept `latest` for the
newest run in the current project.

You can also run in copy mode, fresh mode, or explicit in-place mode:

```bash
deadreckon run "goal" --from .
deadreckon run "goal" --fresh
deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot
```

### Wrap The Agentic CLI You Already Use

deadreckon routes turns through configurable providers. Today, the first-class local CLI adapters are:

- `cli:codex`
- `cli:claude-code`

It also supports direct model routes:

- `anthropic`
- `openai`
- OpenAI-compatible endpoints
- `--smoke` for keyless local verification

That means subscription users can route through supported local agentic CLIs, while API users can route through direct HTTP providers. The CLI does the coding; deadreckon owns the run boundary around it.

### Durable State After Every Turn

Each run writes a complete local record under `~/.deadreckon/runstate/`:

```text
state.json
history.json
events.jsonl
traces.jsonl
spend.jsonl
provenance.jsonl
snapshots/turn-<N>/
proofs/turn-acceptance.json
working/ or promoted library artifact
```

If the terminal dies, the run state is still there. If a provider call completes, the trace is there. If a tool edits a file, the provenance is there.

### Live Attach Without Owning The Process

Start a run, walk away, then attach from another terminal:

```bash
deadreckon attach latest
```

The TUI shows compact run status, phase, goal, working directory, per-turn timer,
spend or context telemetry, provider/tool activity, generated files, process
status, and completion actions. Completed runs can toggle a styled Markdown
rendering of `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` directly in the main panel.

Detach without killing the run:

```text
Ctrl-D
```

### Spend And Wall-Clock Guardrails

Every provider response appends a spend record and updates totals. API routes track token cost. Subscription CLI routes can be capped by wall-clock time.

```bash
deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-spend 15
deadreckon run "large refactor" --max-wall-seconds 1800
```

High spend requires explicit confirmation, so scripts do not accidentally launch expensive runs.

### Per-Turn Undo

deadreckon snapshots the working directory at turn boundaries:

```bash
deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 3
```

This is not just `git reset`. It works against the run's own snapshot trail and records the undo in the run trace.

### Signed Acceptance Gates

The agent cannot declare its own work accepted.

Completion requires a marker written by the separate `dr-gate` binary and bound to the run id with a run-local nonce. deadreckon refuses forged or self-written markers.

Default acceptance checks that the working directory exists and runs `cargo test` when `Cargo.toml` is present. You can add an explicit `acceptance.yaml`:

```yaml
name: notes check
checks:
  - kind: file_exists
    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
  - kind: content_match
    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
    pattern: "dead reckoning"
  - kind: build_success
    cwd: "{working_dir}"
```

Supported check kinds:

```text
cargo_test
file_exists
content_match
build_success
```

### Provenance, Traces, And Run Docs

deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then writes self-documenting artifacts for the completed run:

```bash
deadreckon doc <run-id>
deadreckon doc <run-id> --kind as-built
```

# gnhf: Autonomous Agent Orchestrator – Key Architecture & Mechanics

## Core Purpose
gnhf is an orchestrator that runs agents autonomously in loops while you sleep, committing incremental changes toward an objective. The tagline captures it well: *"Never wake up empty-handed."*

## Iteration Architecture

**The Loop Flow:**
Each iteration follows this pattern:
1. Build a prompt injecting prior `notes.md` context
2. Invoke the agent in non-interactive mode
3. On success: commit the work and append to `notes.md`
4. On failure: reset via `git reset --hard` (except commit failures, which preserve work for repair)

The system tracks three consecutive-failure types: agent-reported failures proceed immediately, retryable hard errors use exponential backoff, and permanent errors abort instantly.

## Commit Semantics

**Incremental & Unsigned:**
"Each successful iteration is a separate unsigned git commit, so you can cherry-pick or revert individual changes without GPG or SSH" interruptions. This design eliminates signing friction during long autonomous runs.

**Failure Preservation:**
If `git commit` itself fails, gnhf preserves the uncommitted work and requests the next iteration repair it rather than losing changes.

## Rollback & Retry Strategy

| Scenario | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Successful iteration | Commit + append notes |
| Agent-reported failure | Roll back, retry immediately |
| Retryable hard error | Roll back, exponential backoff |
| Commit failure | Preserve work, request repair next iteration |
| 3 consecutive failures | Abort + print log path |

## Agent Abstraction

gnhf supports six native agents plus ACP targets:
- **Claude Code:** Native CLI, non-interactive mode
- **Codex, Copilot, Pi:** Each with dedicated invocation patterns
- **Rovo Dev, OpenCode:** Auto-spawned local servers
- **ACP targets:** Bundled `acpx` registry (e.g., `acp:gemini`, custom commands)

All agents output structured results; gnhf treats that as iteration-final and gracefully shuts down lingering processes.

## Worktree Support

Passing `--worktree` isolates each agent run in a separate `git worktree`:

```
<repo>-gnhf-worktrees/
  ├── <run-slug-1>/
  └── <run-slug-2>/
```

This enables **concurrent multi-agent runs** without interference. Preserved worktrees remain after exit for review; empty worktrees auto-remove unless commit-failure repair work is pending.

## Configuration & CLI

**Key Flags:**
- `--max-iterations <n>` – Abort after n total iterations
- `--max-tokens <n>` – Abort after n input+output tokens  
- `--stop-when <condition>` – End when agent reports condition met
- `--prevent-sleep on|off` – Block system sleep during run
- `--current-branch` – Run on existing branch instead of `gnhf/` branch
- `--push` – Push after each successful iteration
- `--agent <agent>` – Select agent (default: config file)

**Config File** (`~/.gnhf/config.yml`):
Stores agent preference, custom binary paths, agent CLI arg overrides, ACP custom targets, commit-message convention (default vs. semantic-release `conventional`), and max consecutive failures (default: 3).

## Exit Summary

After shutdown, gnhf prints a permanent stdout summary with:
- Final branch name
- Elapsed time  
- Iteration and token totals (prefixed `~` = estimate)
- Branch diff stats
- Notes/debug-log file paths
- Review commands

## Token Accounting & Observability

**Token Tracking:**
"Each run writes a JSONL debug log to `.gnhf/runs/<runId>/gnhf.log` alongside `notes.md`" capturing lifecycle events, HTTP requests, and agent streaming output in per-iteration `iteration-<n>.jsonl` files. Token totals in the TUI are prefixed with `~` when estimated.

ACP targets use `used` deltas when available; otherwise gnhf estimates via prompt length and tool-call counts.

## Runtime Caps

- `--max-iterations` stops *before* the next iteration begins
- `--max-tokens` can abort mid-iteration once usage reaches the cap
- `--stop-when` ends after an iteration meeting the condition (unless commit-failure repair is pending first)
- Resumed runs reuse the saved stop condition unless you pass `--stop-when ""` to clear it

## Telemetry & Privacy

"Anonymous usage telemetry" is sent to self-hosted analytics. Crucially: *"No prompts, repo paths, or branch names are sent."* Disable with `GNHF_TELEMETRY=0`.

## Agent Skill Integration

The npm package includes `skills/gnhf/SKILL.md` for agents supporting local skills, documenting *Hands-Off mode* (bounded overnight work) and *Companion mode* (agent-steered long-running orchestration).

---

**Bottom Line:** gnhf abstracts away agent differences via a unified non-interactive interface, manages state through incremental git commits, recovers gracefully from failures, and gives you a clean branch plus a complete audit trail when you wake up.
```

1	# deadreckon Alpha Design
2	
3	## Product
4	
5	`deadreckon` is a Rust 2024 CLI harness for unattended long-running coding tasks. The default user flow is `deadreckon run <goal>`: create durable run state, select a BYOK provider route, execute turns in a disposable sandbox, write spend/provenance/traces/snapshots after every turn, and make the run attachable, resumable, killable, inspectable, and undoable.
6	
7	The alpha implementation is intentionally local-first. Runtime state defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, and tests or explicit smoke runs can override that with `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke` so this build process does not write outside the allowed implementation tree.
8	
9	## Reference Patterns
10	
11	- AS-BUILT §3: two-layer split. Rust owns state, locks, sandboxes, provider routing, and gates. Markdown skills under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/` own agent-facing instructions.
12	- AS-BUILT §4: `state.json` per run, status enum, gap-numbered phase IDs, and `current/<task>.json` run pointers.
13	- AS-BUILT §6: JSON lock records with PID liveness and heartbeat stale reclaim.
14	- AS-BUILT §7-8: atomic promotion/gate markers are written by binary-owned verification, not by model prose.
15	- AS-BUILT §9: per-turn snapshots make bounded rollback possible.
16	- Claude Code mining:
17	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/BashTool/bashPermissions.ts` and `shouldUseSandbox.ts` inform command side-effect boundaries and sandbox warning posture.
18	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/shared/spawnMultiAgent.ts` informs inherited run context for future sub-agent work; alpha records scope and session lineage but leaves explicit forks to V1.
19	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/upstreamproxy/upstreamproxy.ts` informs fail-open provider/proxy setup and child-process environment merging.
20	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/ink/renderer.ts` informs ratatui attach rendering: bounded frames, no uncontrolled terminal state.
21	  - `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/docs/prompts/` informs the Markdown skill shape in `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`.
22	
23	## Workspace
24	
25	Source lives under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`:
26	
27	- `crates/deadreckon-core`: run paths, phase machine, JSON state, codebase mode records, locks, heartbeats, snapshots, provenance, spend, traces, gates, imports.
28	- `crates/deadreckon-providers`: BYOK config at `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, provider trait, Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenAI-compatible, `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, and explicit `--smoke` scripted adapters, fallback routing, spend estimates.
29	- `crates/deadreckon-sandbox`: `sandbox-exec`, `bwrap`, `docker`, and `none` backends using `tokio::process::Command`; default `auto`.
30	- `crates/deadreckon`: clap CLI, ratatui attach UI, init/config/run/status/list/doc/attach/kill/resume/undo/show/import/materialize/export/apply/abandon/discard/cleanup/extend/doctor.
31	- `skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`: Markdown skill loaded at runtime.
32	- `tests/`: workspace integration tests.
33	
34	## Top-10 Need Mapping
35	
36	1. Live Context & Spend Meter: `spend.jsonl` in `deadreckon-core`, spend summaries in `deadreckon attach`.
37	2. Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination: scope hashing, run pointers, and locks in `deadreckon-core`.
38	3. Infinite Undo For Agent Edits: per-turn `snapshots/turn-<N>/` plus `deadreckon undo`.
39	4. Prompt-To-Code Provenance Audit Trail: `provenance.jsonl` and `deadreckon show`.
40	5. Cross-Tool State Sharing: read-only import from `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`, `/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/`, `/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/`.
41	6. Agent Observability: `traces.jsonl` with LLM/tool/sandbox events and latencies.
42	7. Disposable Sandboxes: platform-native sandbox backends, Docker opt-in, `none` warning.
43	8. Billing Guardrails: `--max-spend <USD>` pauses runs when durable spend reaches cap.
44	9. Provider Routing / BYOK: adapters, CLI sub-agents, `deadreckon init`, `deadreckon config get/set`, and fallback chain configured from TOML.
45	10. Workspace Inventory & Run Queue: project-scoped `list`, `status`/`next`, `latest` run aliases, `attach`, `kill`, `resume`, `cleanup`, and state scan commands.
46	
47	## Execution Model
48	
49	The primary path is provider-driven: `deadreckon run <goal>` resolves the
50	codebase mode, previews the plan, creates state, calls `ProviderRouter::complete`,
51	parses model actions, executes tool calls in the configured sandbox, feeds
52	results into history, and repeats until a provider returns `done`, a spend cap
53	pauses the run, or the run is killed. HTTP providers use user-supplied keys or
54	env vars; CLI providers use local subscription CLIs and run through the
55	deadreckon sandbox wrapper.
56	
57	In a git repo, the default codebase mode is `worktree`: deadreckon creates
58	`~/.deadreckon/worktrees/<scope>-<run-id>` on a `dr/...` branch, runs the agent
59	there, and leaves the user's checkout untouched until `deadreckon apply`. Outside
60	git, interactive users can initialize git, copy the directory, or cancel.
61	Non-interactive users must pass `--fresh`, `--from`, or initialize git first.
62	The former empty working directory path remains available as `--fresh`.
63	
64	For keyless local verification only, `deadreckon run --smoke <goal>` selects the `smoke` provider explicitly. That scripted provider still goes through the same turn loop, sandbox dispatch, snapshots, spend records, traces, provenance, and external `dr-gate` acceptance marker; it is not the default run path.
65	
66	The default skill is Markdown and external to the binary. The binary loads it and records the skill name/path in state; it does not parse or mutate skill internals.
67	
68	## CLI Lifecycle
69	
70	Completed artifacts are promoted into `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/`.
71	Worktree runs keep their `dr/...` branch available for review and finish with
72	`deadreckon apply <run-id>` or `deadreckon abandon <run-id>`. `discard` is a
73	friendlier alias for `abandon`. `apply` supports squash, merge, and cherry-pick
74	strategies; `abandon` removes the worktree and, unless `--keep-branch` is used,
75	the temporary branch.
76	
77	Copy and fresh runs use `deadreckon materialize <run-id> --dest <path>` or the
78	`deadreckon export <run-id> --dest <path>` alias to copy the library artifact to
79	a user-owned path, write `.deadreckon/parent.json`, and record the reverse
80	`.materialized-to` marker in the library. `deadreckon extend
81	<run-id> "follow-up goal"` preserves the parent's mode semantics: worktree
82	parents create a child `dr/...` branch off the parent branch, copy/fresh parents
83	seed a new working tree from the parent library, and in-place parents refuse with
84	a direct `run --in-place` hint. Extended runs store parent lineage in
85	`working/.deadreckon/parent.json` and start the normal turn loop with reset
86	resource caps.
87	
88	For normal operation, run ids accept unique prefixes and `latest` / `last`
89	resolve to the most recent run in the current project scope. `deadreckon list`
90	defaults to that current scope, `deadreckon list --all` shows global history, and
91	running `deadreckon` without a subcommand is equivalent to `deadreckon status`.
92	`deadreckon cleanup` / `deadreckon prune` remove abandoned, stale, or explicitly
93	selected completed worktree runs while leaving promoted library artifacts in
94	place.
95	
96	Lineage and codebase mode metadata intentionally stay outside `PipelineState`;
97	show/list/hints derive them from marker files and `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json`
98	so the state schema remains stable.
99	
100	Self-documenting run artifacts also live outside `PipelineState`. Each run
101	starts `working/.deadreckon/docs/`, appends deterministic per-turn records, and
102	attempts one `run-narrator` polish pass before promotion unless `--no-docs` is
103	set. Public copies land under `docs/` in the promoted artifact, and `apply`
104	builds its default commit body from the narrative and decisions docs.
105	
106	## Decisions And Conflicts
107	
108	- Runtime writes during verification: the rider prescribes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, while the build instruction forbids edits outside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` and `/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/goals/`. The binary defaults to `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`, but all repository verification uses `DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.deadreckon-smoke`.
109	- Sub-agent forking: the architecture requires the pattern, but the V1 list explicitly moves `deadreckon fork` to V1. Alpha records scope/session lineage and keeps the subprocess skill boundary; explicit multi-agent forks are documented in `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
110	- Sandbox fallback: on macOS `auto` selects `sandbox-exec` if available. If not available, or on Linux without `bwrap`, `doctor` reports the missing binary and `run` falls back to `none` with a warning, matching the rider.
111	- Live Tier C CLI verification: `codex` was run with `exec --ephemeral --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` inside deadreckon's outer `sandbox-exec` wrapper. Run `59c57e4565704135a9982789d0754803` produced `working/notes.md`, `traces.jsonl`, `provenance.jsonl`, snapshots, and a validated `dr-gate` marker without raw API keys.
112	- First-run UX: `deadreckon init` writes `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`, `deadreckon config get/set` performs non-interactive edits, `doctor` prints actionable check/fix lines, and `run` enforces the `$50` confirmation guard for scripts.
113	- Codebase modes: the architecture keeps mode metadata in
114	  `working/.deadreckon/codebase.json` rather than extending `PipelineState`.
115	  This preserves existing runstate readers while allowing worktree, copy,
116	  in-place, and fresh flows to evolve independently.

```text
# GNHF: Install and Configuration Guide

## Installation Methods

The project offers two primary installation approaches:

**Package Manager Installation:**
"npm install -g gnhf" provides the quickest setup path for most users.

**Source-Based Installation:**
Users preferring development builds can clone the repository, install dependencies with npm, compile using the build script, and create a global symlink via npm link.

## Agent Support

GNHF integrates with multiple AI coding assistants through a unified interface. The system supports Claude Code (Anthropic's native CLI), Codex (OpenAI), GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi, Rovo Dev (via Atlassian), OpenCode, and ACP targets through the bundled acpx registry.

Each agent requires prior installation and authentication. For instance, Claude Code demands "Install Anthropic's claude CLI and sign in first" before gnhf can invoke it in non-interactive mode.

## Configuration System

The tool creates `~/.gnhf/config.yml` on first execution. Key configurable elements include:

- Default agent selection (defaults to Claude)
- Custom binary paths for native agents
- Custom argument injection per agent
- ACP registry overrides for local forks
- Commit message conventions (standard or semantic-release style)
- Maximum consecutive failure threshold
- Sleep prevention toggle

CLI flags override configuration file settings. The iteration and token caps exist only as runtime flags, while `--stop-when` persists per individual run.

## Runtime Flags

Notable command-line options include `--max-iterations` (iteration count limit), `--max-tokens` (token budget), `--stop-when` (natural-language exit condition), `--worktree` (concurrent agent execution), `--current-branch` (in-place operation), and `--push` (post-iteration delivery).

## Telemetry Notice

Usage telemetry transmits anonymized data to support development prioritization. "No prompts, repo paths, or branch names are sent." Users can disable this via the `GNHF_TELEMETRY=0` environment variable.
```

226	                .is_some_and(|cap| state.total_wall_seconds > cap)
227	        {
228	            state.pause_reason = Some("wall-clock cap reached".to_string());
229	            save_state(state)?;
230	            emit_run_completed(
231	                state,
232	                config.event_sender.as_ref(),
233	                RunLoopOutcome::PausedAtCap,
234	            )?;
235	            return Ok(RunLoopOutcome::PausedAtCap);
236	        }
237	
238	        if is_cli_subagent(&response) {
239	            let tool_call_id = format!("cli-subagent-turn-{turn}");
240	            emit_event(
241	                state,
242	                config.event_sender.as_ref(),
243	                RunEventKind::ToolCallStarted {
244	                    turn,
245	                    tool_call_id: tool_call_id.clone(),
246	                    tool_name: "cli_subagent".to_string(),
247	                    args: response.trace.clone(),
248	                },
249	            )?;
250	            let changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(state, turn.saturating_sub(1))?;
251	            if changed.is_empty() {
252	                state.failure_reason =
253	                    Some("cli subagent completed without file changes".to_string());
254	                state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(40), PhaseStatus::Failed)?;
255	                save_state(state)?;
256	                emit_run_completed(state, config.event_sender.as_ref(), RunLoopOutcome::Failed)?;
257	                return Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Failed);
258	            }
259	            snapshot_working(state, turn)?;
260	            append_trace(
261	                state,
262	                &TraceRecord {
263	                    timestamp: Utc::now(),
264	                    run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
265	                    turn,
266	                    event: "tool.cli_subagent".to_string(),
267	                    latency_ms: response
268	                        .trace
269	                        .get("duration_ms")
270	                        .and_then(Value::as_u64)
271	                        .map(u128::from),
272	                    detail: json!({
273	                        "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
274	                        "provider": response.provider,
275	                        "trace": response.trace,
276	                    }),
277	                },
278	            )?;
279	            append_provenance_for_files(
280	                state,
281	                turn,
282	                &tool_call_id,
283	                &response.model,
284	                changed.clone(),
285	            )?;
286	            commit_worktree_turn(state, turn, "cli_subagent")?;
287	            append_turn_doc(
288	                state,
289	                TurnDocInput {
290	                    turn,
291	                    tool_kind: "cli_subagent".to_string(),
292	                    latency_ms: response
293	                        .trace
294	                        .get("duration_ms")
295	                        .and_then(Value::as_u64)
296	                        .map(u128::from),
297	                    files: changed,
298	                    outcome: event_preview(&response.content),
299	                    response_text: response.content.clone(),
300	                },
301	            )?;
302	            emit_event(
303	                state,
304	                config.event_sender.as_ref(),
305	                RunEventKind::ToolCallResult {
306	                    turn,
307	                    tool_call_id,
308	                    status: "ok".to_string(),
309	                    preview: event_preview(&response.content),
310	                },
311	            )?;
312	            state.turn = turn;
313	            complete_run_docs(state, router, &config).await?;
314	            run_acceptance_gate(state)?;
315	            validate_acceptance_marker(state)?;
316	            promote_if_ready(state)?;
317	            state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), PhaseStatus::Completed)?;
318	            save_state(state)?;
319	            emit_run_completed(state, config.event_sender.as_ref(), RunLoopOutcome::Done)?;
320	            return Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Done);
321	        }
322	
323	        let action = parse_action(&response)?;
324	        match action {
325	            Action::Bash {
326	                tool_call_id,
327	                command,
328	            } => {
329	                let tool_token = turn_token.child_token();
330	                emit_event(
331	                    state,
332	                    config.event_sender.as_ref(),
333	                    RunEventKind::ToolCallStarted {
334	                        turn,
335	                        tool_call_id: tool_call_id.clone(),
336	                        tool_name: "bash".to_string(),
337	                        args: tool_args_json(&command),
338	                    },
339	                )?;
340	                let started = Instant::now();
341	                let policy = ToolSandboxPolicy::bash(state.working_dir.clone());
342	                let output = match run_sandbox(SandboxSpec {
343	                    backend: config.sandbox_backend,
344	                    cwd: state.working_dir.clone(),
345	                    program: OsString::from("sh"),
346	                    args: vec![OsString::from("-lc"), OsString::from(command.clone())],
347	                    env: BTreeMap::new(),
348	                    allow_network: policy.allow_network,
349	                    pid_file: Some(
350	                        state
351	                            .run_root
352	                            .join("child-pids")
353	                            .join(format!("tool-{tool_call_id}.pid")),
354	                    ),
355	                    cancellation_token: Some(tool_token),
356	                    profile_dir: Some(state.run_root.join("sandbox")),
357	                    read_allowlist: policy.read_allowlist,
358	                    write_allowlist: policy.write_allowlist,
359	                    network_allowlist: policy.network_allowlist,
360	                })
361	                .await
362	                {
363	                    Ok(output) => output,
364	                    Err(deadreckon_sandbox::SandboxError::Cancelled)
365	                        if should_cancel_run(state, &run_token) =>
366	                    {
367	                        state.status = crate::state::RunStatus::Killed;
368	                        state.failure_reason = Some("run cancelled during tool call".to_string());
369	                        save_state(state)?;
370	                        emit_run_completed(
371	                            state,
372	                            config.event_sender.as_ref(),
373	                            RunLoopOutcome::Killed,
374	                        )?;
375	                        return Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Killed);
376	                    }
377	                    Err(err) => return Err(err.into()),
378	                };
379	                append_trace(
380	                    state,
381	                    &TraceRecord {
382	                        timestamp: Utc::now(),
383	                        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
384	                        turn,
385	                        event: "tool.bash".to_string(),
386	                        latency_ms: Some(started.elapsed().as_millis()),
387	                        detail: json!({
388	                            "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
389	                            "command": command,
390	                            "status_code": output.status_code,
391	                            "stdout": output.stdout,
392	                            "stderr": output.stderr,
393	                            "warning": output.warning,
394	                        }),
395	                    },
396	                )?;
397	                let changed = changed_files_since_snapshot(state, turn.saturating_sub(1))?;
398	                snapshot_working(state, turn)?;
399	                append_provenance_for_files(
400	                    state,
401	                    turn,
402	                    &tool_call_id,
403	                    &response.model,
404	                    changed.clone(),
405	                )?;
406	                commit_worktree_turn(state, turn, &format!("bash {tool_call_id}"))?;
407	                append_turn_doc(
408	                    state,
409	                    TurnDocInput {
410	                        turn,
411	                        tool_kind: "bash".to_string(),
412	                        latency_ms: Some(started.elapsed().as_millis()),
413	                        files: changed,
414	                        outcome: format!("status={:?}", output.status_code),
415	                        response_text: response.content.clone(),
416	                    },
417	                )?;
418	                emit_event(
419	                    state,
420	                    config.event_sender.as_ref(),
421	                    RunEventKind::ToolCallResult {
422	                        turn,
423	                        tool_call_id: tool_call_id.clone(),
424	                        status: format!("{:?}", output.status_code),
425	                        preview: event_preview(format!("{}{}", output.stdout, output.stderr)),
426	                    },
427	                )?;
428	                history.push(format!(
429	                    "tool {tool_call_id} result: status={:?}",
430	                    output.status_code
431	                ));
432	            }
433	            Action::WriteFile {
434	                tool_call_id,
435	                path,
436	                content,
437	            } => {
438	                emit_event(
439	                    state,
440	                    config.event_sender.as_ref(),
441	                    RunEventKind::ToolCallStarted {
442	                        turn,
443	                        tool_call_id: tool_call_id.clone(),
444	                        tool_name: "write_file".to_string(),
445	                        args: tool_args_json(path.display().to_string()),
446	                    },
447	                )?;
448	                let target = match safe_working_path(&state.working_dir, &path) {
449	                    Ok(target) => target,
450	                    Err(err) => {
451	                        let reason = err.to_string();
452	                        append_tool_refusal(
453	                            state,
454	                            turn,
455	                            &tool_call_id,
456	                            "write_file",
457	                            &response.model,
458	                            &reason,
459	                            config.event_sender.as_ref(),
460	                        )?;
461	                        history.push(format!("tool {tool_call_id} refused: {reason}"));
462	                        state.turn = turn;
463	                        save_history(state, &history)?;
464	                        save_state(state)?;
465	                        continue;
466	                    }
467	                };
468	                if let Some(parent) = target.parent() {
469	                    std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
470	                }
471	                std::fs::write(&target, content).with_path(&target)?;
472	                append_trace(
473	                    state,
474	                    &TraceRecord {
475	                        timestamp: Utc::now(),
476	                        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
477	                        turn,
478	                        event: "tool.write_file".to_string(),
479	                        latency_ms: None,
480	                        detail: json!({
481	                            "tool_call_id": tool_call_id,
482	                            "path": target,
483	                        }),
484	                    },
485	                )?;
486	                snapshot_working(state, turn)?;
487	                let changed = vec![target.clone()];
488	                append_provenance_for_files(
489	                    state,
490	                    turn,
491	                    &tool_call_id,
492	                    &response.model,
493	                    changed.clone(),
494	                )?;
495	                commit_worktree_turn(state, turn, &format!("write_file {tool_call_id}"))?;
496	                append_turn_doc(
497	                    state,
498	                    TurnDocInput {
499	                        turn,
500	                        tool_kind: "write_file".to_string(),
501	                        latency_ms: None,
502	                        files: changed,
503	                        outcome: "ok".to_string(),
504	                        response_text: response.content.clone(),
505	                    },
506	                )?;
507	                emit_event(
508	                    state,
509	                    config.event_sender.as_ref(),
510	                    RunEventKind::ToolCallResult {
511	                        turn,
512	                        tool_call_id: tool_call_id.clone(),
513	                        status: "ok".to_string(),
514	                        preview: "wrote file".to_string(),
515	                    },
516	                )?;
517	                history.push(format!("tool {tool_call_id} result: wrote file"));
518	            }
519	            Action::Done { summary } => {
520	                state.turn = turn;
521	                append_turn_doc(
522	                    state,
523	                    TurnDocInput {
524	                        turn,
525	                        tool_kind: "done".to_string(),
526	                        latency_ms: None,
527	                        files: Vec::new(),
528	                        outcome: summary.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "done".to_string()),
529	                        response_text: response.content.clone(),
530	                    },
531	                )?;
532	                complete_run_docs(state, router, &config).await?;
533	                run_acceptance_gate(state)?;
534	                validate_acceptance_marker(state)?;
535	                promote_if_ready(state)?;
536	                state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(60), PhaseStatus::Completed)?;
537	                save_state(state)?;
538	                history.push(format!("done: {}", summary.unwrap_or_default()));
539	                save_history(state, &history)?;
540	                emit_run_completed(state, config.event_sender.as_ref(), RunLoopOutcome::Done)?;
541	                return Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Done);
542	            }
543	        }
544	        state.turn = turn;
545	        save_history(state, &history)?;
546	        save_state(state)?;
547	    }
548	
549	    state.failure_reason = Some("max turn budget exhausted".to_string());
550	    state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(40), PhaseStatus::Failed)?;
551	    save_state(state)?;
552	    emit_run_completed(state, config.event_sender.as_ref(), RunLoopOutcome::Failed)?;
553	    Ok(RunLoopOutcome::Failed)
554	}
555	
556	fn should_cancel_run(state: &PipelineState, token: &CancellationToken) -> bool {
557	    state.status == RunStatus::Killed || token.is_cancelled() || cancel_marker_present(state)
558	}
559	
560	struct CancelMarkerGuard {
561	    shutdown: CancellationToken,
562	    handle: tokio::task::JoinHandle<()>,
563	}
564	
565	impl CancelMarkerGuard {
566	    fn spawn(run_root: PathBuf, run_token: CancellationToken) -> Self {
567	        let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
568	        let shutdown_for_task = shutdown.clone();
569	        let marker = cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(&run_root);
570	        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
571	            loop {
572	                tokio::select! {
573	                    _ = shutdown_for_task.cancelled() => break,
574	                    _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)) => {
575	                        if marker.exists() {
576	                            run_token.cancel();
577	                            break;
578	                        }
579	                    }
580	                }
581	            }
582	        });
583	        Self { shutdown, handle }
584	    }
585	}
586	
587	impl Drop for CancelMarkerGuard {
588	    fn drop(&mut self) {
589	        self.shutdown.cancel();
590	        self.handle.abort();
591	    }
592	}
593	
594	fn emit_run_completed(
595	    state: &PipelineState,
596	    sender: Option<&broadcast::Sender<RunEvent>>,
597	    outcome: RunLoopOutcome,
598	) -> Result<()> {
599	    let status = match outcome {
600	        RunLoopOutcome::Done => "completed",
601	        RunLoopOutcome::PausedAtCap => "paused",
602	        RunLoopOutcome::Killed => "killed",
603	        RunLoopOutcome::Failed => "failed",
604	    };
605	    emit_event(
606	        state,
607	        sender,
608	        RunEventKind::RunCompleted {
609	            status: status.to_string(),
610	        },
611	    )
612	}

646	fn parse_action(response: &ProviderResponse) -> Result<Action> {
647	    serde_json::from_str(&response.content).map_err(|err| {
648	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
649	            "provider returned non-action JSON: {err}; content={}",

659	fn safe_working_path(root: &Path, relative: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf> {
660	    if relative.is_absolute()
661	        || relative
662	            .components()
663	            .any(|part| matches!(part, std::path::Component::ParentDir))
664	    {
665	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
666	            "unsafe write path {}",
667	            relative.display()
668	        )));
669	    }
670	    Ok(root.join(relative))
671	}
672	
673	fn changed_files_since_snapshot(state: &PipelineState, snapshot_turn: u32) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>> {
674	    let snapshot_dir = state
675	        .run_root
676	        .join("snapshots")
677	        .join(format!("turn-{snapshot_turn}"));
678	    let before = file_set(&snapshot_dir)?;
679	    let after_files = inventory_files(&state.working_dir)?;
680	    let mut changed = Vec::new();
681	    for file in after_files {
682	        let relative = file.strip_prefix(&state.working_dir).map_err(|err| {
683	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("working path prefix error: {err}"))
684	        })?;
685	        let before_path = snapshot_dir.join(relative);
686	        if !before.contains(relative) || file_bytes(&file)? != file_bytes(&before_path)? {
687	            changed.push(file);
688	        }
689	    }
690	    Ok(changed)
691	}
692	
693	fn file_set(root: &Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<PathBuf>> {
694	    Ok(inventory_files(root)?
695	        .into_iter()
696	        .filter_map(|path| path.strip_prefix(root).ok().map(Path::to_path_buf))
697	        .collect())
698	}
699	
700	fn file_bytes(path: &Path) -> Result<Vec<u8>> {
701	    match std::fs::read(path) {
702	        Ok(bytes) => Ok(bytes),
703	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(Vec::new()),
704	        Err(source) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
705	            path: path.to_path_buf(),
706	            source,
707	        }),
708	    }
709	}

784	fn load_history(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
785	    let path = history_path(state);
786	    if !path.exists() {
787	        return Ok(Vec::new());
788	    }
789	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
790	    serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json { path, source })
791	}
792	
793	fn save_history(state: &PipelineState, history: &[String]) -> Result<()> {
794	    let path = history_path(state);
795	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
796	        std::fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
797	    }
798	    let data = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(history).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
799	        path: path.clone(),
800	        source,
801	    })?;
802	    std::fs::write(&path, data).with_path(&path)
803	}
804	
805	fn history_path(state: &PipelineState) -> PathBuf {
806	    state.run_root.join("history.json")
807	}
808	
809	fn load_or_reconstruct_history(
810	    state: &mut PipelineState,
811	    from_turn: Option<u32>,
812	) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
813	    let trace_reconstruction = reconstruct_history_from_traces(state)?;
814	    let history_exists = history_path(state).exists();
815	    let mut history = if history_exists {
816	        load_history(state)?
817	    } else {
818	        trace_reconstruction.history
819	    };
820	    if let Some(from_turn) = from_turn {
821	        history.truncate(from_turn as usize);
822	        state.turn = from_turn;
823	        truncate_run_artifacts_after_turn(state, from_turn)?;
824	        save_history(state, &history)?;
825	        save_state(state)?;
826	    } else if !history_exists && trace_reconstruction.last_complete_turn > state.turn {
827	        state.turn = trace_reconstruction.last_complete_turn;
828	        save_history(state, &history)?;
829	        save_state(state)?;
830	    }
831	    Ok(history)
832	}
833	
834	struct ReconstructedHistory {
835	    history: Vec<String>,
836	    last_complete_turn: u32,
837	}
838	
839	fn reconstruct_history_from_traces(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<ReconstructedHistory> {
840	    let path = state.run_root.join("traces.jsonl");
841	    if !path.exists() {
842	        return Ok(ReconstructedHistory {
843	            history: Vec::new(),
844	            last_complete_turn: 0,
845	        });
846	    }
847	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(&path).with_path(&path)?;
848	    let mut complete_lines = Vec::new();
849	    let mut history = Vec::new();
850	    let mut last_complete_turn = 0;
851	    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
852	        let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
853	            break;
854	        };
855	        complete_lines.push(line.to_string());
856	        let event = value
857	            .get("event")
858	            .and_then(Value::as_str)
859	            .unwrap_or_default();
860	        let turn = value
861	            .get("turn")
862	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
863	            .unwrap_or_default() as u32;
864	        if is_completed_tool_trace(event)
865	            && let Some(tool_call_id) = value
866	                .pointer("/detail/tool_call_id")
867	                .and_then(Value::as_str)
868	        {
869	            history.push(format!(
870	                "tool {tool_call_id} result: reconstructed from trace"
871	            ));
872	            last_complete_turn = last_complete_turn.max(turn);
873	        }
874	    }
875	    let sanitized = complete_lines.join("\n");
876	    if sanitized.len() != raw.trim_end_matches('\n').len() {
877	        std::fs::write(
878	            &path,
879	            if sanitized.is_empty() {
880	                String::new()
881	            } else {
882	                format!("{sanitized}\n")
883	            },
884	        )
885	        .with_path(&path)?;
886	    }
887	    Ok(ReconstructedHistory {
888	        history,
889	        last_complete_turn,
890	    })
891	}

893	fn is_completed_tool_trace(event: &str) -> bool {
894	    matches!(event, "tool.bash" | "tool.write_file" | "tool.cli_subagent")
895	}

897	fn truncate_run_artifacts_after_turn(state: &PipelineState, from_turn: u32) -> Result<()> {
898	    for name in ["traces.jsonl", "spend.jsonl"] {
899	        truncate_jsonl_after_turn(&state.run_root.join(name), from_turn)?;
900	    }
901	    let snapshots = state.run_root.join("snapshots");
902	    if let Ok(entries) = std::fs::read_dir(&snapshots) {
903	        for entry in entries.flatten() {
904	            let path = entry.path();
905	            let Some(turn) = path
906	                .file_name()
907	                .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
908	                .and_then(|name| name.strip_prefix("turn-"))
909	                .and_then(|turn| turn.parse::<u32>().ok())
910	            else {
911	                continue;
912	            };
913	            if turn > from_turn {
914	                std::fs::remove_dir_all(&path).with_path(&path)?;
915	            }
916	        }
917	    }
918	    Ok(())
919	}
920	
921	fn truncate_jsonl_after_turn(path: &Path, from_turn: u32) -> Result<()> {
922	    if !path.exists() {
923	        return Ok(());
924	    }
925	    let raw = std::fs::read_to_string(path).with_path(path)?;
926	    let mut kept = Vec::new();
927	    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
928	        let Ok(value) = serde_json::from_str::<Value>(line) else {
929	            break;
930	        };
931	        if value
932	            .get("turn")
933	            .and_then(Value::as_u64)
934	            .is_none_or(|turn| turn <= u64::from(from_turn))
935	        {
936	            kept.push(line.to_string());
937	        }
938	    }
939	    std::fs::write(
940	        path,
941	        if kept.is_empty() {
942	            String::new()
943	        } else {
944	            format!("{}\n", kept.join("\n"))
945	        },
946	    )
947	    .with_path(path)
948	}

955	async fn complete_run_docs(
956	    state: &mut PipelineState,
957	    router: &ProviderRouter,
958	    config: &RunLoopConfig,
959	) -> Result<()> {
960	    let owned_router = if let (Some(config_path), Some(doc_provider)) = (
961	        config.docs.config_path.as_ref(),
962	        config.docs.doc_provider.as_deref(),
963	    ) {
964	        ProviderRouter::from_config_path(config_path, Some(doc_provider)).ok()
965	    } else {
966	        None
967	    };
968	    let router = owned_router.as_ref().unwrap_or(router);
969	    let previous_status = state.status;
970	    state.status = RunStatus::Completed;
971	    let result = polish_run_docs(
972	        state,
973	        router,
974	        &PolishConfig {
975	            home: config.docs.home.clone(),
976	            doc_skill: config.docs.doc_skill.clone(),
977	            doc_provider: config.docs.doc_provider.clone(),
978	            no_llm: config.docs.no_docs,
979	            force: false,
980	        },
981	    )
982	    .await;
983	    state.status = previous_status;
984	    result
985	}

987	fn paths_for_state(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<DeadreckonPaths> {
988	    let home = state
989	        .run_root
990	        .parent()
991	        .and_then(Path::parent)
992	        .and_then(Path::parent)
993	        .and_then(Path::parent)
994	        .ok_or_else(|| {
995	            DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
996	                "cannot infer home from run root {}",
997	                state.run_root.display()
998	            ))
999	        })?;
1000	    Ok(DeadreckonPaths::from_home(home))
1001	}

1011	fn run_acceptance_gate(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<()> {
1012	    let gate = gate_binary_path()?;
1013	    let output = std::process::Command::new(&gate)
1014	        .arg("--run")
1015	        .arg(&state.run_id)
1016	        .arg("--run-root")
1017	        .arg(&state.run_root)
1018	        .arg("--working-dir")
1019	        .arg(&state.working_dir)
1020	        .output()
1021	        .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
1022	            path: gate.clone(),
1023	            source,
1024	        })?;
1025	    if !output.status.success() {
1026	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
1027	            "dr-gate failed: {}{}",
1028	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
1029	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
1030	        )));
1031	    }
1032	    Ok(())
1033	}

1035	fn commit_worktree_turn(state: &PipelineState, turn: u32, label: &str) -> Result<()> {
1036	    let record = match read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir) {
1037	        Ok(record) => record,
1038	        Err(_) => return Ok(()),
1039	    };
1040	    if record.mode != CodebaseMode::Worktree {
1041	        return Ok(());
1042	    }
1043	    git_status(
1044	        &state.working_dir,
1045	        &["config", "user.email", "deadreckon@example.invalid"],
1046	    )?;
1047	    git_status(&state.working_dir, &["config", "user.name", "deadreckon"])?;
1048	    git_status(&state.working_dir, &["add", "-A"])?;
1049	    if git_quiet(&state.working_dir, &["diff", "--cached", "--quiet"])? {
1050	        return Ok(());
1051	    }
1052	    git_status(
1053	        &state.working_dir,
1054	        &["commit", "-m", &format!("turn {turn}: {label}")],
1055	    )
1056	}
1057	
1058	fn git_quiet(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<bool> {
1059	    let output = Command::new("git")
1060	        .arg("-C")
1061	        .arg(cwd)
1062	        .args(args)
1063	        .output()
1064	        .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
1065	            path: PathBuf::from("git"),
1066	            source,
1067	        })?;
1068	    Ok(output.status.success())
1069	}
1070	
1071	fn git_status(cwd: &Path, args: &[&str]) -> Result<()> {
1072	    let output = Command::new("git")
1073	        .arg("-C")
1074	        .arg(cwd)
1075	        .args(args)
1076	        .output()
1077	        .map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
1078	            path: PathBuf::from("git"),
1079	            source,
1080	        })?;
1081	    if output.status.success() {
1082	        Ok(())
1083	    } else {
1084	        Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
1085	            "git {:?} failed: {}{}",
1086	            args,
1087	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
1088	            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
1089	        )))
1090	    }
1091	}
1092	
1093	fn gate_binary_path() -> Result<PathBuf> {
1094	    let current = std::env::current_exe().map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
1095	        path: PathBuf::from("/Users/gdc/deadreckon/target"),
1096	        source,
1097	    })?;
1098	    let gate = current.with_file_name("dr-gate");
1099	    if gate.exists() {
1100	        return Ok(gate);
1101	    }
1102	    Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
1103	        "dr-gate binary next to {}",
1104	        current.display()
1105	    )))
1106	}

342	function readCommitMessageMetadata(

346	  if (value === "" || value === "default") return undefined;
347	  if (value === "conventional") return CONVENTIONAL_COMMIT_MESSAGE;
348	  throw new Error(`Unknown commit message metadata: ${value}`);

351	function inferCommitMessageFromSchema(
352	  schemaPath: string,
353	): CommitMessageConfig | undefined {
354	  if (!existsSync(schemaPath)) return undefined;
355	  try {
356	    const schema = JSON.parse(readFileSync(schemaPath, "utf-8")) as {
357	      properties?: Record<string, unknown>;
358	    };
359	    if (
360	      schema.properties?.type !== undefined &&
361	      schema.properties.scope !== undefined
362	    ) {
363	      return CONVENTIONAL_COMMIT_MESSAGE;
364	    }
365	  } catch {
366	    // Legacy metadata is best-effort; malformed schemas fall back to default.
367	  }
368	  return undefined;
369	}

410	function ensureRunMetadataIgnored(cwd: string): void {
411	  const excludePath = execFileSync(
412	    "git",
413	    ["rev-parse", "--git-path", "info/exclude"],
414	    { cwd, encoding: "utf-8" },
415	  ).trim();
416	  const resolved = isAbsolute(excludePath)
417	    ? excludePath
418	    : join(cwd, excludePath);
419	  const entry = ".gnhf/runs/";
420	  mkdirSync(dirname(resolved), { recursive: true });
421	
422	  if (existsSync(resolved)) {
423	    const content = readFileSync(resolved, "utf-8");
424	    if (content.split("\n").some((line) => line.trim() === entry)) return;
425	    const separator = content.length > 0 && !content.endsWith("\n") ? "\n" : "";
426	    appendFileSync(resolved, `${separator}${entry}\n`, "utf-8");
427	  } else {
428	    // This ignore rule is runtime metadata, so keep it local to the clone
429	    // instead of mutating tracked .gitignore state on startup.
430	    writeFileSync(resolved, `${entry}\n`, "utf-8");
431	  }
432	}

506	import {

510	
511	export function buildIterationPrompt(params: {
512	  n: number;
513	  runId: string;
514	  prompt: string;
515	  stopWhen?: string;
516	  commitMessage?: CommitMessageConfig;
517	}): string {
518	  const outputFields = [
519	    "- success: whether you were able to make a meaningful contribution that got us closer towards the objective. setting this to false means any code change you made should be discarded. A complete no-op iteration (no file changes AND no new meaningful learnings worth recording) is not a success - set success=false so the run can halt rather than spin on no-op iterations",
520	    "- summary: a concise one-sentence summary of the accomplishment in this iteration",
521	    "- key_changes_made: an array of descriptions for key changes you made. don't group this by file - group by logical units of work. don't describe activities - describe material outcomes",
522	    "- key_learnings: an array of new learnings that were surprising, weren't captured by previous notes and would be informative for future iterations",
523	  ];
524	
525	  for (const field of getCommitMessagePromptFields(params.commitMessage)) {
526	    const constraints = [
527	      field.allowed === undefined
528	        ? null
529	        : `allowed values: ${field.allowed.join(", ")}`,
530	      `default: ${JSON.stringify(field.default)}`,
531	    ].filter((value): value is string => value !== null);
532	    outputFields.push(
533	      `- ${field.name}: ${field.description}. ${constraints.join("; ")}`,
534	    );
535	  }
536	
537	  if (params.stopWhen !== undefined) {
538	    outputFields.push(
539	      "- should_fully_stop: set to true ONLY when the stop condition below is fully met and the entire loop should end. default to false",
540	    );
541	  }
542	
543	  const stopConditionSection =
544	    params.stopWhen !== undefined
545	      ? `\n\n## Stop Condition\n\nThe user has configured a condition to end the loop: ${params.stopWhen}\nIf this condition is fully met after this iteration's work, set should_fully_stop=true in your output. Otherwise set it to false.`
546	      : "";
547	
548	  return `You are working autonomously towards an objective given below.
549	This is iteration ${params.n}. Each iteration aims to make an incremental step forward, not to complete the entire objective.
550	
551	## Instructions
552	
553	1. Read .gnhf/runs/${params.runId}/notes.md first to understand what has been done in previous iterations. Do NOT write to or modify notes.md - it is maintained automatically by the gnhf orchestrator
554	2. Identify the next smallest logical unit of work that's individually verifiable and would make incremental progress towards the objective, and treat that as the scope of this iteration
555	3. If you attempted a solution and it didn't end up moving the needle on the objective, document learnings and record success=false, then conclude the iteration rather than continuously pivoting
556	4. If you made code changes, run build/tests/linters/formatters if available to validate your work. Do NOT make any git commits - that will be handled automatically by the gnhf orchestrator
557	5. If you started any long-running background processes (dev servers, browsers, watchers, Electron, etc.), stop them before finishing the iteration
558	6. Only submit the final JSON object after the result is final: your work is complete, validation is done, and you have stopped any background processes you started
559	
560	## Output
561	
562	${outputFields.join("\n")}${stopConditionSection}
563	
564	## Objective
565	
566	${params.prompt}`;
567	}

618	    green: (text: string) => wrap("\x1b[32m", text),
619	    red: (text: string) => wrap("\x1b[31m", text),
620	    magenta: (text: string) => wrap("\x1b[35m", text),

629	function padVisible(text: string, width: number): string {

632	
633	function truncateVisible(text: string, width: number): string {
634	  if (visibleLength(text) <= width) return text;
635	  if (width <= 0) return "";
636	
637	  const targetWidth = Math.max(0, width - 1);
638	  let output = "";
639	  let visible = 0;
640	  let index = 0;
641	  let hasActiveStyle = false;
642	  const finish = () => `${output}…${hasActiveStyle ? "\x1b[0m" : ""}`;
643	
644	  for (const match of text.matchAll(ANSI_TOKEN_RE)) {
645	    const chunk = text.slice(index, match.index);
646	    for (const char of chunk) {
647	      if (visible >= targetWidth) return finish();
648	      output += char;
649	      visible += 1;
650	    }
651	    output += match[0];
652	    hasActiveStyle = match[0] !== "\x1b[0m";
653	    index = match.index! + match[0].length;
654	  }
655	
656	  for (const char of text.slice(index)) {
657	    if (visible >= targetWidth) return finish();
658	    output += char;
659	    visible += 1;
660	  }
661	
662	  return finish();
663	}

665	function formatDuration(ms: number): string {

669	  const seconds = totalSeconds % 60;
670	  if (hours > 0) return `${hours}h ${minutes}m`;
671	  if (minutes > 0) return `${minutes}m ${seconds}s`;
672	  return `${seconds}s`;
673	}

817	export interface AgentOutputSchema {
818	  type: "object";
819	  additionalProperties: false;
820	  properties: Record<
821	    string,
822	    { type: string; items?: { type: string }; enum?: string[] }
823	  >;
824	  required: string[];
825	}
826	
827	function isRecord(value: unknown): value is Record<string, unknown> {
828	  return typeof value === "object" && value !== null && !Array.isArray(value);
829	}
830	
831	function describeSchemaType(name: string, type: string): string {
832	  const article = /^[aeiou]/.test(type) ? "an" : "a";
833	  return `${name} must be ${article} ${type}`;
834	}
835	
836	export function validateAgentOutput(
837	  value: unknown,
838	  schema: AgentOutputSchema,
839	): AgentOutput {
840	  if (!isRecord(value)) {
841	    throw new Error("expected an object");
842	  }
843	
844	  if (schema.additionalProperties === false) {
845	    const allowed = new Set(Object.keys(schema.properties));
846	    const extraKey = Object.keys(value).find((key) => !allowed.has(key));
847	    if (extraKey) {
848	      throw new Error(`unexpected property ${extraKey}`);
849	    }
850	  }
851	
852	  for (const name of schema.required) {
853	    if (!(name in value)) {
854	      throw new Error(`${name} is required`);
855	    }
856	  }
857	
858	  for (const [name, property] of Object.entries(schema.properties)) {
859	    if (!(name in value)) {
860	      continue;
861	    }
862	    const propertyValue = value[name];
863	
864	    if (property.type === "array") {
865	      if (
866	        !Array.isArray(propertyValue) ||
867	        property.items?.type !== "string" ||
868	        !propertyValue.every((item) => typeof item === "string")
869	      ) {
870	        throw new Error(`${name} must be an array of strings`);
871	      }
872	      continue;
873	    }
874	
875	    if (typeof propertyValue !== property.type) {
876	      throw new Error(describeSchemaType(name, property.type));
877	    }
878	
879	    if (property.enum && !property.enum.includes(propertyValue as string)) {
880	      throw new Error(
881	        `${name} must be one of ${property.enum.map((item) => JSON.stringify(item)).join(", ")}`,
882	      );
883	    }
884	  }
885	
886	  return value as unknown as AgentOutput;
887	}

889	export interface AgentOutputCommitField {
890	  name: string;
891	  allowed?: string[];
892	}

894	// Codex's --output-schema enforces OpenAI strict mode, which requires every
895	// key in `properties` to also appear in `required` when additionalProperties
896	// is false. So include should_fully_stop only when the run actually uses it.
897	export function buildAgentOutputSchema(opts: {
898	  includeStopField: boolean;
899	  commitFields?: AgentOutputCommitField[];
900	}): AgentOutputSchema {
901	  const properties: AgentOutputSchema["properties"] = {
902	    success: { type: "boolean" },
903	    summary: { type: "string" },
904	    key_changes_made: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
905	    key_learnings: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } },
906	  };
907	  const required = ["success", "summary", "key_changes_made", "key_learnings"];
908	  for (const field of opts.commitFields ?? []) {
909	    properties[field.name] = {
910	      type: "string",
911	      ...(field.allowed === undefined ? {} : { enum: field.allowed }),
912	    };
913	    required.push(field.name);
914	  }
915	  if (opts.includeStopField) {
916	    properties.should_fully_stop = { type: "boolean" };
917	    required.push("should_fully_stop");
918	  }
919	  return {
920	    type: "object",
921	    additionalProperties: false,
922	    properties,
923	    required,
924	  };
925	}

1086	// Bounded in-memory buffer so events emitted before a run's log file is
1087	// known (e.g. sleep-prevention spawn events) aren't lost. Flushed to disk
1088	// once initDebugLog is called.
1089	const PRE_INIT_BUFFER_CAPACITY = 1000;
1090	const STACK_LINE_LIMIT = 12;
1091	const CAUSE_DEPTH_LIMIT = 6;

1093	let logPath: string | null = null;

1097	function formatLine(event: string, details: Record<string, unknown>): string {
1098	  const base = {
1099	    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
1100	    pid: process.pid,
1101	    event,
1102	  };
1103	  // Logging is best-effort and runs from timer callbacks, EventEmitter
1104	  // handlers, and error paths — throwing here would turn diagnostic output
1105	  // into an uncaught exception. JSON.stringify can throw on BigInts,
1106	  // circular references, or Error subclasses with throwing getters, so we
1107	  // fall back to a minimal line that at least records the event name.
1108	  try {
1109	    return `${JSON.stringify({ ...base, ...details })}\n`;
1110	  } catch (error) {
1111	    return `${JSON.stringify({
1112	      ...base,
1113	      logError:
1114	        error instanceof Error
1115	          ? `${error.name}: ${error.message}`
1116	          : String(error),
1117	      detailsKeys: Object.keys(details),
1118	    })}\n`;
1119	  }
1120	}
1121	
1122	export function initDebugLog(path: string): void {
1123	  logPath = path;
1124	  try {
1125	    mkdirSync(dirname(path), { recursive: true });
1126	  } catch {
1127	    // Best-effort: the directory usually already exists.
1128	  }
1129	
1130	  if (preInitBuffer.length === 0 && preInitDroppedCount === 0) return;
1131	
1132	  // If any events were dropped while the buffer was full, prepend a sentinel
1133	  // so the log makes it obvious that early events are missing instead of
1134	  // silently losing them.
1135	  const droppedSentinel =
1136	    preInitDroppedCount > 0
1137	      ? formatLine("debug-log:pre-init-overflow", {
1138	          droppedCount: preInitDroppedCount,
1139	          bufferCapacity: PRE_INIT_BUFFER_CAPACITY,
1140	        })
1141	      : "";
1142	  const flushed = droppedSentinel + preInitBuffer.join("");
1143	  preInitBuffer = [];
1144	  preInitDroppedCount = 0;
1145	  try {
1146	    appendFileSync(path, flushed, "utf-8");
1147	  } catch {
1148	    // Debug logging is best-effort only.
1149	  }
1150	}
1151	
1152	export function appendDebugLog(
1153	  event: string,

1318	// characters like `, $, ", ', and ; are harmless data rather than executable
1319	// syntax. Do not add a code path that builds a shell command string from

1327	function git(

1429	export interface BranchDiffStats {
1430	  commits: number;
1431	  filesChanged: number;
1432	  filesAdded: number;
1433	  filesUpdated: number;
1434	  filesDeleted: number;
1435	  filesRenamed: number;
1436	  binaryFiles: number;

1438	  linesDeleted: number;
1439	}
1440	
1441	function emptyBranchDiffStats(): BranchDiffStats {
1442	  return {
1443	    commits: 0,
1444	    filesChanged: 0,
1445	    filesAdded: 0,
1446	    filesUpdated: 0,
1447	    filesDeleted: 0,

1449	    binaryFiles: 0,
1450	    linesAdded: 0,
1451	    linesDeleted: 0,
1452	  };

1454	
1455	export function getBranchDiffStats(
1456	  baseCommit: string,
1457	  cwd: string,
1458	): BranchDiffStats {
1459	  if (!baseCommit) return emptyBranchDiffStats();
1460	
1461	  const range = `${baseCommit}..HEAD`;
1462	  const stats = emptyBranchDiffStats();
1463	  stats.commits = Number.parseInt(
1464	    git(["rev-list", "--count", "--first-parent", range], cwd),
1465	    10,
1466	  );
1467	
1468	  const nameStatus = git(["diff", "--name-status", range], cwd);
1469	  for (const line of nameStatus.split("\n")) {
1470	    if (!line) continue;
1471	    const [status] = line.split("\t");
1472	    stats.filesChanged++;
1473	    if (status === "A") {
1474	      stats.filesAdded++;
1475	    } else if (status === "D") {
1476	      stats.filesDeleted++;
1477	    } else if (status?.startsWith("R")) {
1478	      stats.filesUpdated++;
1479	      stats.filesRenamed++;
1480	    } else {
1481	      stats.filesUpdated++;
1482	    }
1483	  }
1484	
1485	  const numstat = git(["diff", "--numstat", range], cwd);
1486	  for (const line of numstat.split("\n")) {
1487	    if (!line) continue;
1488	    const [added, deleted] = line.split("\t");
1489	    if (added === "-" || deleted === "-") {
1490	      stats.binaryFiles++;
1491	      continue;
1492	    }
1493	    stats.linesAdded += Number.parseInt(added ?? "0", 10) || 0;
1494	    stats.linesDeleted += Number.parseInt(deleted ?? "0", 10) || 0;
1495	  }
1496	
1497	  return stats;
1498	}

1514	=== skills/gnhf/SKILL.md ===
1515	---
1516	name: gnhf
1517	description: Use when the user asks to run GNHF, says they are going to sleep or leaving and wants an agent-managed coding run, asks to supervise, steer, or review an active GNHF run, or gives feedback on GNHF results.
1518	---
1519	
1520	# GNHF
1521	
1522	## Overview
1523	
1524	GNHF is an agent orchestrator: it repeatedly calls another coding agent until a natural-language stop condition is met. This skill teaches the host agent to prepare one durable run and, in Companion mode, steer or review it.
1525	
1526	Core rule: the host agent orchestrates; GNHF executes. Do not manually implement inside the same scope while a GNHF worker is responsible for it unless the user explicitly changes the delegation.
1527	
1528	In Companion mode, GNHF completion is not user acceptance. "Stop condition met" only means the worker stopped; the host still compares the result to the user's latest requirements and fresh verification.
1529	
1530	## Modes
1531	
1532	Choose exactly one mode for the run.
1533	
1534	### Hands-Off
1535	
1536	Use when the task is bounded, verification is clear, and the user wants one configured run to proceed without steering.
1537	
1538	- Prepare a precise prompt with constraints, non-goals, verification, and stop condition.
1539	- Launch GNHF and wait for completion.
1540	- Intervene early only for hard failure, runaway scope, destructive behavior, or impossible prerequisites.
1541	- Report the final GNHF status after exit.
1542	
1543	Examples:
1544	
1545	- English: "I'm going to bed. Use GNHF with Copilot to keep working on this branch and stop when the test suite passes."
1546	- Chinese: "我要睡了。用 GNHF 接着跑这个分支，测试都过了就停。"
1547	
1548	### Companion
1549	
1550	Use when the task is uncertain, exploratory, design-heavy, research-heavy, or likely to need course correction.
1551	
1552	Default to Companion when the user asks to iterate until satisfied, requests multi-round work, provides review findings, asks for design/skill/documentation improvement, or asks for supervision.
1553	
1554	- Keep a note of original intent, branch, session id, and last known result.
1555	- Poll the active GNHF process until exit or until an intervention point appears.
1556	- Intervene when the worker optimizes the wrong thing, repeats failed fixes, skips requested research, drifts scope, or claims success without evidence.
1557	- Treat review findings as the next acceptance criteria.
1558	- Prefer a new bounded GNHF prompt over manually taking over implementation.
1559	
1560	Examples:
1561	
1562	- English: "Run GNHF for a few rounds on this onboarding flow. Check the diff between rounds and tighten the next prompt if it starts polishing the wrong thing."
1563	- Chinese: "用 GNHF 多跑几轮这个 onboarding 流程。每轮看一下 diff，如果它开始改偏了，就收窄下一轮 prompt。"
1564	
1565	## Launch
1566	
1567	Check the installed CLI before relying on flags:
1568	
1569	```bash
1570	gnhf --help
1571	```
1572	
1573	Known shape:
1574	
1575	```bash
1576	gnhf \
1577	  --agent <claude|codex|rovodev|opencode|copilot|pi|acp:<target>> \
1578	  --max-iterations <n> \
1579	  --stop-when "<observable completion condition>" \
1580	  --prevent-sleep on \
1581	  "<worker prompt>"
1582	```
1583	
1584	If GNHF has no `--model` flag, put model requirements in the worker prompt or backend config. Do not invent unsupported flags.
1585	
1586	Before launch:
1587	
1588	```bash
1589	git status --short
1590	git branch --show-current
1591	git log --oneline --max-count=5
1592	```
1593	
1594	Prompt skeleton:
1595	
1596	```text
1597	Objective: <one concrete outcome>.
1598	
1599	Use <agent/model requirement>. Work in this repo. Treat this as a long-running GNHF task.
```

1607	
1608	## Steer
1609	
1610	In Companion mode, evaluate after each iteration or meaningful output chunk:
1611	
1612	| Signal                                                        | Action                                                               |
1613	| ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1614	| Worker found a real blocker                                   | Stop or relaunch with blocker-specific instructions                  |
1615	| Good partial slice                                            | Let it continue or tighten the next stop condition                   |
1616	| Skipped requested research                                    | Relaunch with research as explicit first deliverable                 |
1617	| Worker changes unrelated files                                | Stop and review before continuing                                    |
1618	| Worker claims success without verification                    | Review immediately; relaunch only with evidence-based stop condition |
1619	| Reviewer finds a blocking issue or user says not satisfactory | Relaunch with that finding as the sole bounded correction            |
1620	
1621	Steering prompt:
1622	
1623	```text
1624	Continue from the current repo state. The previous run partially succeeded: <evidence>.
1625	
1626	Do not redo completed work. Focus only on <bounded correction>.
1627	
1628	The issue to fix now is <specific observed issue>. Verify with <commands/checks>.
1629	
1630	Stop only when <observable condition>.
1631	```
1632	
1633	## Companion Review
1634	
1635	Use only in Companion mode, when the host is supervising quality or deciding whether to continue with another bounded run.
1636	
1637	1. Inspect branch, status, commits, changed files, and diff.
1638	2. Read GNHF notes/logs as claims, not evidence.
1639	3. Run independent verification: tests, lint, build, typecheck, manual QA, or domain-specific checks.
1640	4. Compare the result to the stop condition and the user's latest feedback.
1641	5. Decide: **Mergeable**, **Needs follow-up GNHF run**, or **Do not merge**.
1642	
1643	If the result needs follow-up, continue in Companion mode instead of presenting the run as complete. Do not merge unless explicitly authorized.
1644	
1645	## Findings
1646	
1647	Use when the user provides findings such as "not preserved", "scope drift", "missing requirement", or "why did you stop".
1648	
1649	1. Treat the run as Companion mode.
1650	2. Convert each finding into an observable correction. Preserve severity, file/line scope, and the user's wording.
1651	3. Relaunch on the same candidate branch when salvageable.
1652	4. Prompt the worker to fix only the bounded finding, preserve completed valid work, verify, and stop only when the finding is no longer true.
1653	5. Review again after the follow-up.
1654	6. Repeat until no blocking findings remain, verification passes, or a real blocker is found.
1655	
1656	## Morning Review
1657	
1658	Use when the user returns with "good morning", "how did last night's run go?", or similar after a GNHF run.
1659	
1660	Do not ask what to review first. Reconstruct state:
1661	
1662	```bash
1663	git status --short
1664	git branch --show-current
1665	git log --oneline --decorate --max-count=20
1666	pgrep -fl 'gnhf|claude|codex|copilot|opencode|rovodev' || true
1667	```
1668	
1669	Inspect likely GNHF branches, notes, logs, terminal sessions, and changed files. If a GNHF process is still running, report that first.
1670	
1671	Report mode, agent, branch, status, changes, verification, stop-condition result, quality assessment, and recommended next action. Never summarize an overnight run from memory.
1672	
1673	## Agent
1674	
1675	- `copilot`: explicit GitHub Copilot CLI request or local Copilot config.
1676	- `codex`: repo-aware code work or review-heavy tasks.
1677	- `claude`: reasoning-heavy implementation or prose-heavy planning when configured.
1678	- `pi`: explicit Pi request or local Pi configuration.
1679	- `opencode` / `rovodev`: explicit request or repo-specific setup.
1680	- `acp:<target>`: explicit ACP target request, or when the user wants to drive a custom ACP-compatible agent through GNHF.
1681	
1682	## Safety
1683	
1684	- Preserve user changes. Never run destructive git commands to clean up a GNHF branch.
1685	- In Companion mode, do not trust a worker's success summary without fresh verification.
1686	- Keep prompts outcome-based and evidence-based.
1687	- Use concrete stop conditions. Bad: "looks good". Good: "the target workflow succeeds, relevant checks pass, and no unrelated files changed."
1688	- If the user is away, produce branches and a status report, not irreversible changes, unless explicitly authorized.

1745	function shouldUseWindowsShell(
1746	  bin: string,
1747	  platform: NodeJS.Platform,
1748	): boolean {
1749	  if (platform !== "win32") {
1750	    return false;
1751	  }
1752	
1753	  if (/\.(cmd|bat)$/i.test(bin)) {
1754	    return true;
1755	  }

1757	  if (/[\\/]/.test(bin)) {
1758	    return false;
